experiment: Spectral training, native command coverage and controlled input replay

training_spectrum_audit.coefficient_rule: Median of 0.25 * ordinary/frequency output-gradient L2 norms on all 62 training frames; fixed before training and validation.
limitations: Fourier energy describes squared RGB error, not a perceptual or causal diagnosis.
The coefficient balances output-space gradients at the trained control; parameter-gradient balance during training is not guaranteed.
Only training first-reset images are inspected. No optimizer steps, sample or game launches.

mechanical_tests.scope: Gradient is checked with the adaptive spectrum weights held fixed, as defined by the loss; no finite-difference claim for differentiating those weights.

architecture.type: four-level hierarchical residual CNN with global context gate
architecture.input_receptive_field_pixels: whole image via global context gate
architecture.internal_downsampling: learned features only; original pixels retained through input rearrangement and residual path

decoder_conditioning.source: spatial mean of deepest encoder features, before the original context gate
decoder_conditioning.application: per-channel value*(1+scale)+shift after upsample/skip combination at all three decoder stages

limitations: Thirty scene slots and thirty-two photo slots from sixteen training identities. The last sixteen slots use native emission 1.0 captures. Paired mean training gives equal scene/photo weight. Seven different photo identities stay in validation. First-reset static frames only, not game or temporal acceptance.
No temporal training or quality validation.
Torch timing excludes D3D12 integration and is not a hidden-demo benchmark.

output_grading.scope: Unfitted algebraic approximation from the same runtime controls; other camera views reuse the parameters by inference.
output_grading.training: Differentiable FP32 operations after the clamped learned residual.
output_grading.inference: FP16 network, FP32 grading, FP16 final storage; all included in graph timing.

residual_tests.scope: Finite FP16 patterns in selected operand combinations, not every possible triple.

conditioning_tests.scope: Finite half patterns in selected operand combinations, not every possible combination. Explicit round-to-nearest per operation.

limitations: Finite-input equivalence to existing student arithmetic, not native quality.
Complete student graph timings exclude D3D12 integration and do not accelerate native NVIDIA execution.
Exact full-image results cover only the checked checkpoints, inputs and environment.
Intervals average ten consecutive graph replays; p95 is an interval-average percentile, not per-frame tail latency.
Measured execution of experimental students plus grade, excluding D3D12 integration. No native-runtime acceleration.
One static input and one device; other desktop GPU work is not controlled.

paired_capture.scope: Four static fenced frames check observer equality, not temporal/game quality. Observer CPU timings include logging and cannot measure batching benefit.

limitations: Hooks cover the observed ID3D12GraphicsCommandList10 implementations, excluding IUnknown/object methods; existing hooks cover both barrier methods.
Device/resource methods, cached alternative implementations, future interfaces and implicit driver operations are not a complete captured API stream.
Packed CPU argument bytes are copied and retained through process exit; this does not extend embedded GPU-resource lifetimes.
Original argument storage is inspected only while each caller supplies it. Reuse is determined by identity and comparison with an owned earlier copy.
A frame with identical current inputs but different preceding inputs is not an output-equivalence test of identical temporal history.
No kernel calls are merged and no native speedup is claimed. Unmatched-input frames cannot establish output equivalence.

controlled_input_replay.scope: Fixed captured input/control sequence from reset; compare native calls, method tracing with original arguments, and tracing with copied arguments. No kernel batching or timing-speedup claim.

recoveries: Initial command collector stopped before any launch because a capture-DLL filename was incorrect; its corrected path matched the pinned hash.

Replay collector stopped after the completed native-reference trial due to missing audit metadata fields. The corrected collector revalidated that saved capture and resumed only the two missing modes.
limitations: The spectral auxiliary loss worsens all three validation group means. It is rejected and remains off by default.
Sixty-two training and sixteen static validation frames do not establish representative game or temporal quality. Validation is repeatedly consulted during research.
The gradient coefficient is fixed from training-only output gradients; its balance does not necessarily transfer to parameter gradients throughout optimization.
Student graph timings include full-1080p network and grade but exclude application integration; ten replays are averaged per interval.
The preliminary native pair has no matching history from reset. Its current-input-only frame match is inconclusive.
The controlled replay supplies identical color/depth/motion, controls and observed preprocessor noise counters from reset for four frames; both tracing modes match native output exactly.
Command tracing covers the observed interface implementations, not every possible device/resource operation or implicit driver action.
Argument copies are retained to process exit. Embedded GPU-resource lifetime and error handling must still be preserved by any future batcher.
No native kernel calls are merged or accelerated. Five sample launches stayed on the inactive private desktop; no game or driver changes.
